integration_issues.issue: axios validateStatus prevents JS exception but browser still logs 'Failed to load resource: 401' at the network layer — hyper-user opening DevTools console will still see 2 red 401 entries for /api/auth/me on anon /dashboard visit. The PATCH B claim is technically incomplete. Fix options: (a) backend returns 200 {user: null} for anon instead of 401; (b) frontend skips fetchMe() when document.cookie lacks 'session_token'.

action_items: PATCH B: To truly silence the 401 console noise, either (a) make /api/auth/me return 200 with null body for anon OR (b) in AuthProvider check(), skip fetchMe() entirely when document.cookie does not contain 'session_token'. The current axios validateStatus is necessary but insufficient — Chromium logs the 401 at the network layer independently of axios.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthProvider check() calls fetchMe() unconditionally on every mount, including anon visits — this is architecturally the source of the 401 noise. Consider a cookie-presence guard.
React StrictMode is likely causing the /auth/me call to fire twice (2 identical 401 console entries observed) — expected in dev but doubles the noise.

rca_of_the_issue: PATCH B RCA: axios `validateStatus: (s) => s === 200 || s === 401` only tells axios not to throw a JS Error when status is 401; it does NOT suppress the browser's own network-error logging. Chromium's network stack unconditionally writes 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 ()' to devtools console for ANY HTTP 4xx/5xx response, regardless of how the fetch/XHR consumer handles it. Reproduction: fresh incognito context → GET https://audit-engine-38.preview.emergentagent.com/dashboard → open DevTools Console → 2× red 'Failed to load resource: 401' entries pointing at /api/auth/me. Mitigation: either backend returns 200 with body {user: null} for anonymous requests, or AuthProvider.check() gates fetchMe() behind `document.cookie.includes('session_token')`.
